title: Interview
summary: Pick a concept, answer 10 interview questions, then check your score.

lessons.title: JavaScript: let, const, and var
english: Question: What is the difference between let, const, and var?
let and const belong to the block they are written in. var belongs to the function. const cannot be reassigned. let can. Prefer const, then let. Avoid var in new code.
hindi: Question: let, const, aur var mein kya farq hai?

let aur const usi block mein rehte hain jahan likhe gaye hain. var function tak rehta hai. const ko dubara assign nahi kar sakte. let ko kar sakte hain. Naye code mein const, phir let. var avoid karo.

lessons.title: JavaScript: == and ===
english: Question: Why do interviewers prefer ===?
=== checks value and type. == converts types first, so 1 == "1" is true and bugs hide. 1 === "1" is false. Use === unless you have a clear reason not to.
hindi: Question: Interviewer === ko kyun pasand karte hain?
=== value aur type dono check karta hai. == pehle type badalta hai, isliye 1 == "1" true ho jata hai aur bug chhup jata hai. 1 === "1" false hai. Bina wajah == mat use karo.

lessons.title: React: props and state
english: Question: What is the difference between props and state?
Props come from the parent and the child should not change them. State is data the component owns. Call the setter from useState to change it. React then renders the new UI.
hindi: Question: Props aur state mein kya farq hai?
Props parent se aate hain aur child unhe nahi badalta. State woh data hai jo component ke paas hai. Badalne ke liye useState ka setter call karo. React naya UI render karta hai.

lessons.title: React: why lists need keys
english: Question: Why does a list need a key?
React uses the key to match items when the list changes. A stable id from the data is a good key. The array index is a weak key when items are inserted, moved, or deleted.
hindi: Question: List ko key kyun chahiye?
Jab list badalti hai, React key se item pehchanta hai. Data ki stable id achhi key hai. Index kamzor key hai jab items beech mein add, move, ya delete hote hain.

lessons.title: Node.js: what it is for
english: Question: What is Node.js used for?

Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser. People use it for APIs, servers, and tools. It is built on V8 and handles slow work, like the network, through an event loop instead of blocking the process.
hindi: Question: Node.js kis kaam ke liye use hota hai?
Node.js JavaScript ko browser ke bahar chalata hai. Isse APIs, servers, aur tools bante hain. Ye V8 par bana hai. Network jaisa slow kaam event loop se hota hai, poori process rukti nahi.

lessons.title: Next.js: server and client components
english: Question: When do you add use client?

In the app router, components are server components unless the file starts with use client. Add that directive when the component needs state, effects, or browser events. Keep it as low in the tree as you can.
hindi: Question: use client kab likhte hain?

App router mein component server component hota hai, jab tak file use client se shuru na ho. State, effects, ya browser events chahiye hon to ye directive likho. Ise tree mein jitna neeche ho sake, utna neeche rakho.

lessons.title: React Native: View and Text
english: Question: Why is there no div in React Native?
React Native draws native views, not HTML. View is the box. Text is the only place for words. A string directly inside a View does not work the way text inside a div does on the web.
hindi: Question: React Native mein div kyun nahi hota?
React Native HTML nahi, native views banata hai. View box hai. Words sirf Text ke andar likhte hain. View ke andar seedha string web ke div ki tarah kaam nahi karti.

lessons.title: MongoDB: documents
english: Question: How is a MongoDB document different from a table row?
A document is a set of fields, stored as JSON-like data. Documents in one collection can have different shapes. Every document has an _id. A collection is the group of related documents.
hindi: Question: MongoDB document table ki row se kaise alag hai?
Document fields ka set hai, JSON jaisa. Ek collection ke documents ka shape alag ho sakta hai. Har document ka _id hota hai. Collection related documents ka group hai.

lessons.title: Mongoose: schema and populate
english: Question: What do a schema and populate do?

A schema describes fields, types, and rules such as required. MongoDB itself will store almost any shape. The schema rejects bad data in your app. populate replaces a stored id with the related document when you query.
hindi: Question: Schema aur populate kya karte hain?

Schema fields, types, aur rules batata hai, jaise required. MongoDB khud lagbhag koi bhi shape rakh leta hai. Schema galat data ko app mein reject karta hai. populate query ke time stored id ki jagah related document laga deta hai.

title: Node.js
summary: A full Node.js path: runtime, modules, async, core APIs, HTTP, Express, APIs, and advanced process tools.

lessons.title: What Node.js is
english: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser. The same language you use on a page can read files, talk to a database, and serve an API.

It is built on Chrome's V8 engine and uses an event loop. Slow work, like a network call, does not freeze the rest of the program. Node continues with other tasks and comes back when the result is ready.
A typical start is a single file, started with node app.js. From there you add packages and split the app into modules.
hindi: Node.js JavaScript ko browser ke bahar chalata hai. Wahi language jo page par chalti hai, files padh sakti hai, database se baat kar sakti hai, aur API serve kar sakti hai.
Ye Chrome ke V8 engine par bana hai aur event loop use karta hai. Network call jaisa slow kaam baaki program ko rokta nahi. Node dusre kaam karta rehta hai, aur result aane par wapas aata hai.
Shuruaat aksar ek file se hoti hai, node app.js se. Uske baad packages aur alag modules add hote hain.

lessons.title: Node.js and the browser
english: Browser JavaScript can touch the page, DOM, and window. Node.js has no DOM. It can read files, open ports, and talk to the operating system.
Globals differ too. The browser has window and document. Node has global, process, and Buffer. A package written for one host often needs a check before it runs in the other.
hindi: Browser JavaScript page, DOM, aur window ko chhu sakta hai. Node.js mein DOM nahi hota. Ye files padh sakta hai, ports khol sakta hai, aur operating system se baat kar sakta hai.
Globals bhi alag hain. Browser mein window aur document hain. Node mein global, process, aur Buffer hain. Jo package ek host ke liye likha hai, doosre par chalane se pehle check karo.

lessons.title: V8, libuv, and the thread pool
english: V8 runs your JavaScript. libuv provides the event loop and async I/O. Together they let Node accept more work while a disk or network call is still waiting.

Some work, such as file system calls and DNS, uses a small libuv thread pool. The JavaScript you write still runs on one main thread. Heavy CPU loops block that thread, so they belong in worker threads.
hindi: V8 aapka JavaScript chalata hai. libuv event loop aur async I/O deta hai. Dono milkar Node ko aur kaam lene dete hain jab disk ya network call abhi wait kar rahi ho.

Kuch kaam, jaise file system aur DNS, chhote libuv thread pool par jaate hain. Aapka JavaScript phir bhi ek main thread par chalta hai. Bhari CPU loop us thread ko rok deti hai, isliye wo worker threads mein honi chahiye.

lessons.title: process, argv, and the environment
english: process is the handle for the running program. process.argv is the command and its arguments. process.env holds environment variables such as PORT.
process.exit ends the program with a status code. 0 means success. Anything else means failure. process.cwd is the folder the command was started from.
hindi: process chalte hue program ka handle hai. process.argv command aur uske arguments hain. process.env mein PORT jaise environment variables hote hain.
process.exit program ko status code ke saath band karta hai. 0 ka matlab success hai. Uske alawa failure. process.cwd woh folder hai jahan se command start hui.

lessons.title: Modules and npm
english: Node treats each file as a module. In modern Node you export with export and import with import. Older code uses module.exports and require. Pick one style and stay with it.
npm is the package manager that ships with Node. npm init creates package.json, which lists your app name and dependencies. npm install express adds a library and records it.
Never commit node_modules. Share package.json and package-lock.json so someone else can install the same versions.
hindi: Node har file ko ek module maanta hai. Naye Node mein export aur import use hote hain. Purana code module.exports aur require use karta hai. Ek style choose karke usi par raho.
npm Node ke saath aane wala package manager hai. npm init package.json banata hai, jisme app ka naam aur dependencies likhe hote hain. npm install express library add karta hai.
node_modules ko git mein mat daalo. package.json aur package-lock.json share karo, taaki doosra insaan wahi versions install kar sake.

lessons.title: CommonJS require
english: Older Node code uses CommonJS. module.exports sends a value out of the file. require loads it. require is synchronous and resolves from node_modules or a relative path.
Do not mix require and import in the same file unless you know the package type. New apps should prefer ES modules. You will still meet require in many tutorials and older packages.
hindi: Purana Node code CommonJS use karta hai. module.exports file se value bahar bhejta hai. require use load karta hai. require synchronous hai aur node_modules ya relative path se file dhoondhta hai.
Jab tak package type clear na ho, ek hi file mein require aur import mat milao. Naye apps ES modules prefer karein. Purane packages aur tutorials mein require ab bhi milega.
lessons.code:
const { add } = require("./math");
module.exports = { add };

lessons.title: ES modules
english: ES modules use import and export. Enable them with "type": "module" in package.json, or use the .mjs extension. Imports of your own files need the file extension, such as ./math.js.
import is static, so tools can see dependencies. Dynamic import() loads a module later and returns a promise. Node built-ins can be imported as node:fs or node:http.
hindi: ES modules import aur export use karte hain. package.json mein "type": "module" likho, ya .mjs extension use karo. Apni files ke import mein extension chahiye, jaise ./math.js.
import static hota hai, isliye tools dependencies dekh sakte hain. Dynamic import() module baad mein load karta hai aur promise deta hai. Node built-ins node:fs ya node:http se import hote hain.
lessons.code:
import fs from "node:fs/promises";

const text = await fs.readFile("./note.txt", "utf8");

lessons.title: package.json and scripts
english: package.json names the app, sets the module type, and lists dependencies. dependencies are needed to run. devDependencies are needed only while building or testing.

scripts are short commands. npm run dev can start the server. The lock file records exact versions so the next install matches. Semantic versions use major.minor.patch. A major bump can break callers.
hindi: package.json app ka naam, module type, aur dependencies likhta hai. dependencies chalane ke liye chahiye. devDependencies sirf build ya test ke liye.

scripts chhote commands hain. npm run dev server start kar sakta hai. Lock file exact versions rakhta hai taaki agla install wahi ho. Semantic version major.minor.patch hota hai. Major bump callers ko tod sakta hai.

lessons.title: Callbacks
english: A callback is a function you pass so it can run later, when the work finishes. Node's older APIs use an error-first callback: the first argument is an error or null, then the result.
Nested callbacks become hard to read. That shape is called callback hell. Promises and async functions were added so the same flow can be written as steps.
hindi: Callback woh function hai jo aap baad mein chalane ke liye dete ho, jab kaam khatam ho. Node ke purane APIs error-first callback use karte hain: pehla argument error ya null, phir result.
Andar-andar callbacks padhna mushkil ho jata hai. Ise callback hell kehte hain. Promises aur async functions isi flow ko steps ki tarah likhne ke liye aaye.

lessons.title: Promises in Node
english: A promise settles later with a value or an error. then handles success. catch handles failure. The fs/promises module is the promise form of the file APIs.
Promise.all runs several independent jobs and waits for all of them. If one rejects, the combined promise rejects. Use it when the jobs do not depend on each other.
hindi: Promise baad mein value ya error ke saath settle hota hai. then success handle karta hai. catch failure handle karta hai. fs/promises file APIs ka promise form hai.
Promise.all kai independent kaam chalata hai aur sab ka intezar karta hai. Ek reject ho to poora promise reject hota hai. Jab kaam ek doosre par depend na karein, tab use karo.

lessons.title: async and await
english: async marks a function that returns a promise. await pauses that function until the promise settles. The rest of the process keeps running.
Put awaited calls that can fail in try and catch. An unhandled rejection can crash the process, depending on the Node version and flags. Always handle the failure path of network and file calls.
hindi: async function promise return karta hai. await us function ko rokta hai jab tak promise settle na ho. Baaki process chalta rehta hai.
Jo awaited call fail ho sakti hai, use try aur catch mein rakho. Unhandled rejection process ko crash kar sakti hai. Network aur file calls ka failure path hamesha handle karo.

lessons.title: Event loop phases
english: The event loop is a cycle of phases. Timers run setTimeout and setInterval callbacks. The poll phase waits for I/O. The check phase runs setImmediate. Close callbacks run when a handle closes.
process.nextTick and resolved promises run between phases, before the loop continues. A tight nextTick loop can starve I/O. Do not use it to spin forever.
hindi: Event loop phases ka cycle hai. Timers setTimeout aur setInterval callbacks chalate hain. Poll phase I/O ka intezar karti hai. Check phase setImmediate chalati hai. Close callbacks tab chalte hain jab handle band hota hai.
process.nextTick aur resolved promises phases ke beech chalte hain. Tight nextTick loop I/O ko bhookha rakh sakti hai. Use hamesha ke liye ghumao mat.

lessons.title: Timers
english: setTimeout runs once after a delay. setInterval repeats. clearTimeout and clearInterval cancel them. The delay is a minimum, not a promise of the exact millisecond, because other work may be on the loop.
setImmediate runs after the current poll phase. It is useful when you want to yield so I/O callbacks can run before more JavaScript.
hindi: setTimeout ek baar delay ke baad chalta hai. setInterval dohrata hai. clearTimeout aur clearInterval unhe cancel karte hain. Delay minimum hai, exact millisecond ka promise nahi, kyunki loop par aur kaam ho sakta hai.
setImmediate current poll phase ke baad chalta hai. Jab aap JavaScript se pehle I/O callbacks ko mauka dena chahte ho, ye useful hai.

lessons.title: fs: files and folders
english: Import the promise API with import fs from "node:fs/promises". Import the callback and sync API with import fs from "node:fs". A promise method returns a promise. A Sync method blocks the main thread until the disk answers. In a server, use the promise or callback form.

File methods: readFile(path, encoding) reads a file. writeFile replaces the file. appendFile adds to the end. copyFile copies. cp copies a file or a folder. rename moves or renames. unlink deletes a file. rm deletes a file or folder, and { recursive: true } deletes a folder tree. truncate shrinks a file. open returns a handle. close closes it. read and write work on that handle.

Folder and info methods: mkdir creates a folder. Use { recursive: true } for nested folders. mkdtemp makes a unique temporary folder. readdir lists names. opendir walks a folder. stat and lstat return size, mode, and times. access checks that a path is usable. chmod and chown change mode and owner. utimes changes times. realpath resolves symlinks. symlink, link, and readlink manage links. watch and watchFile report changes. unwatchFile stops watchFile. existsSync is the sync existence check. exists is old and should not be used. createReadStream and createWriteStream stream a file. glob finds paths by a pattern.
Output: after writeFileSync("note.txt", "hello") and readFileSync("note.txt", "utf8"), the console prints hello. existsSync("note.txt") prints true.
hindi: Promise API ke liye import fs from "node:fs/promises" likho. Callback aur sync API ke liye import fs from "node:fs". Promise method promise deta hai. Sync method main thread ko rokta hai. Server mein promise ya callback form use karo.

File methods: readFile file padhta hai. writeFile file replace karta hai. appendFile end mein jodta hai. copyFile copy karta hai. cp file ya folder copy karta hai. rename move ya rename karta hai. unlink file delete karta hai. rm file ya folder delete karta hai, aur { recursive: true } poora folder tree hataata hai. truncate file chhota karta hai. open handle deta hai. close use band karta hai. read aur write us handle par kaam karte hain.

Folder methods: mkdir folder banata hai. Nested folders ke liye { recursive: true }. mkdtemp unique temporary folder banata hai. readdir naam list karta hai. stat aur lstat size, mode, aur time dete hain. access path usable hai ya nahi check karta hai. chmod aur chown mode aur owner badalte hain. realpath symlink resolve karta hai. symlink, link, aur readlink links sambhalte hain. watch changes batata hai. existsSync sync existence check hai. exists purana hai, use mat karo. createReadStream aur createWriteStream file stream karte hain. glob pattern se paths dhoondhta hai.
Output: writeFileSync("note.txt", "hello") ke baad readFileSync hello print karta hai. existsSync("note.txt") true print karta hai.

lessons.title: path: build file paths
english: Import it with import path from "node:path". It builds paths so you do not hard-code slashes. path.win32 always uses Windows rules. path.posix always uses forward slashes. The default path follows the operating system you are on.

Methods: join(...parts) cleans and joins segments. resolve(...parts) makes an absolute path from the current folder. normalize cleans . and .. and repeated slashes. isAbsolute tells you if a path starts from the root. relative(from, to) builds the path from one place to another. dirname returns the folder. basename(path, ext) returns the file name, and the optional ext strips that extension. extname returns the extension, including the dot. parse splits a path into root, dir, base, ext, and name. format builds a path back from that object. matchesGlob checks a path against a pattern. sep is the slash character. delimiter is the PATH separator, semicolon on Windows and colon elsewhere.
Output: path.posix.basename("/data/note.txt") prints note.txt. path.posix.extname prints .txt. path.posix.dirname prints /data. path.posix.join("data", "note.txt") prints data/note.txt.
hindi: Import path from "node:path" se import karo. Ye paths banata hai taaki aap slash hard-code na karo. path.win32 hamesha Windows rules use karta hai. path.posix hamesha forward slash use karta hai. Default path aapke operating system ka hota hai.

Methods: join segments jodta hai. resolve current folder se absolute path banata hai. normalize . aur .. saaf karta hai. isAbsolute batata hai path root se shuru hai ya nahi. relative ek jagah se doosri jagah ka path banata hai. dirname folder deta hai. basename file ka naam deta hai. extname extension deta hai, dot ke saath. parse path ko root, dir, base, ext, aur name mein todta hai. format us object se path wapas banata hai. matchesGlob pattern check karta hai. sep slash character hai. delimiter PATH separator hai.
Output: basename note.txt print karta hai. extname .txt print karta hai. dirname /data print karta hai. join data/note.txt print karta hai.

lessons.title: events: EventEmitter methods
english: Import it with import { EventEmitter } from "node:events". An emitter is an object that can announce named events. HTTP servers, streams, and many other Node objects inherit this behavior.

Methods: on(event, listener) and addListener subscribe. once subscribes for a single call. prependListener and prependOnceListener put the listener at the front. emit(event, ...args) runs the listeners and returns true if at least one ran. off and removeListener remove one listener. You must pass the same function you subscribed. removeAllListeners(event) clears one event, or every event if you omit the name. listeners and rawListeners return the current list. listenerCount returns how many there are. eventNames returns the names that still have listeners. setMaxListeners and getMaxListeners control the warning limit. The default warning appears around 10 listeners. The special error event crashes the process if you emit it and nobody is listening.
Output: the example prints ok, then true, then 0, then false. emit returns true when a listener ran. listenerCount is 0 because once already removed itself. The second emit returns false.
hindi: Import { EventEmitter } from "node:events" se import karo. Emitter woh object hai jo naam wale events announce kar sakta hai. HTTP servers aur streams isi behavior ko inherit karte hain.

Methods: on aur addListener subscribe karte hain. once sirf ek baar chalta hai. prependListener listener ko aage lagata hai. emit listeners chalata hai aur true deta hai agar koi listener tha. off aur removeListener ek listener hataate hain. Wahi function do jo subscribe kiya tha. removeAllListeners sab hata deta hai. listeners list deta hai. listenerCount count deta hai. eventNames naam deta hai. setMaxListeners warning limit set karta hai. error event sunne wala na ho to process crash ho sakti hai.
Output: example ok print karta hai, phir true, phir 0, phir false. emit true deta hai jab listener chala. listenerCount 0 hai kyunki once khud hat chuka hai. Doosra emit false deta hai.

lessons.title: buffer: bytes and encodings
english: Buffer is global in Node, so you can use it without an import. It holds raw bytes. A string is text. A buffer is the bytes behind that text, a file, or a network packet.

Constructors and static methods: Buffer.from(value, encoding) creates a buffer from a string, array, or another buffer. Buffer.alloc(size, fill) creates a zeroed or filled buffer. Buffer.allocUnsafe(size) is faster but may contain old memory, so fill it before use. Buffer.concat(list, totalLength) joins buffers. Buffer.isBuffer(value) checks the type. Buffer.compare(a, b) sorts buffers. Buffer.byteLength(string, encoding) counts bytes, which is not always the same as string length. Buffer.isEncoding checks a name such as utf8, hex, base64, or latin1.

Instance methods: buf.toString(encoding) decodes bytes. buf.write(string, offset, encoding) writes into an existing buffer. buf.copy(target) copies bytes. buf.subarray(start, end) is a view of the same memory. buf.slice is the older name. buf.equals checks same bytes. buf.compare orders two buffers. buf.indexOf, buf.lastIndexOf, and buf.includes search. buf.fill fills a range. buf.readUInt8, buf.readUInt16BE, buf.readUInt32BE, buf.readInt8, and the matching write methods read and write numbers. LE means little-endian and BE means big-endian. buf.swap16 and buf.swap32 swap byte order. buf.toJSON returns { type: "Buffer", data: [...] }.
Output: Buffer.from("hello").toString("hex") prints 68656c6c6f. Buffer.byteLength("hello") prints 5. "hello".length is also 5, but a character such as é can be more than one byte.
hindi: Buffer Node mein global hai, isliye bina import ke chal jata hai. Ye raw bytes rakhta hai. String text hai. Buffer un bytes ko rakhta hai jo file ya network packet mein hote hain.

Static methods: Buffer.from string ya array se buffer banata hai. Buffer.alloc size ka saaf buffer banata hai. Buffer.allocUnsafe tez hai par purani memory ho sakti hai. Buffer.concat buffers jodta hai. Buffer.isBuffer type check karta hai. Buffer.byteLength bytes ginata hai, jo hamesha string length nahi hota. Encodings utf8, hex, base64, aur latin1 hain.

Instance methods: toString bytes ko text banata hai. write existing buffer mein likhta hai. copy bytes copy karta hai. subarray usi memory ka view hai. equals same bytes check karta hai. indexOf aur includes search karte hain. fill range bharta hai. readUInt8 aur write methods numbers padhte aur likhte hain. BE big-endian hai aur LE little-endian.
Output: hello ka hex 68656c6c6f hai. byteLength 5 hai.

lessons.title: stream: chunked data
english: Import classes from "node:stream" and pipeline from "node:stream/promises". A stream moves data in chunks so a large file never has to sit fully in memory.

Classes: Readable produces chunks. Writable accepts them. Duplex is both. Transform changes chunks as they pass. PassThrough is a Duplex that does not change the bytes. Readable.from(array) turns an array or async iterable into a readable stream.

Readable methods: read, pause, resume, pipe, unpipe, unshift, wrap, destroy, destroyed, readableEnded. Events include data, end, error, and close. Writable methods: write, end, cork, uncork, destroy. write returns false when the buffer is full. Wait for the drain event before writing more. That waiting is backpressure. Transform implements _transform and optional _flush.

Helpers: pipeline(source, ...transforms, destination) connects streams and forwards errors. finished(stream) resolves when a stream ends or errors. stream.compose chains transforms. stream.duplexPair makes a connected pair. stream.addAbortSignal cancels a stream from an AbortSignal.
Output: piping a readable stream of the letters a and b into process.stdout prints ab. pipeline from in.txt to out.txt copies the file and prints nothing when it succeeds.
hindi: Classes "node:stream" se import karo aur pipeline "node:stream/promises" se. Stream data ko chunks mein chalata hai taaki badi file poori memory mein na aaye.
Classes: Readable chunks banata hai. Writable unhe leta hai. Duplex dono hai. Transform beech mein badalta hai. PassThrough bytes ko nahi badalta. Readable.from array ko stream bana deta hai.
Readable methods: read, pause, resume, pipe, unpipe, destroy. Writable methods: write, end, cork, uncork. write false deta hai jab buffer full ho. drain event ka intezar karo. Yahi backpressure hai.
Helpers: pipeline streams jodta hai aur errors aage bhejta hai. finished tab resolve hota hai jab stream khatam ho. compose transforms jodta hai.
Output: a aur b ki stream stdout par ab print karti hai. pipeline file copy karta hai aur success par kuch print nahi karta.

lessons.title: os: the operating system
english: Import it with import os from "node:os". It reads facts about the machine. It does not change system settings.

Methods: arch() is the CPU architecture, such as x64 or arm64. platform() is win32, darwin, or linux. type(), release(), version(), and machine() describe the operating system. hostname() is the computer name. homedir() is the user home folder. tmpdir() is the temporary folder. userInfo() returns username, uid, gid, shell, and homedir. endianness() is LE or BE. cpus() returns one object per logical CPU, with model and speed. freemem() and totalmem() are byte counts. availableParallelism() is a suggested worker count. uptime() is seconds since boot. loadavg() is the 1, 5, and 15 minute load on Unix, and zeros on Windows. networkInterfaces() lists addresses. constants holds signal numbers and priority values. getPriority and setPriority read and change the process priority.
Output: os.platform() prints win32 on Windows, darwin on macOS, and linux on Linux. os.arch() often prints x64 or arm64. The exact strings depend on the computer.
hindi: Import os from "node:os" se import karo. Ye machine ki jaankari padhta hai. Ye system settings nahi badalta.

Methods: arch() CPU architecture hai, jaise x64 ya arm64. platform() win32, darwin, ya linux hai. hostname() computer ka naam hai. homedir() user ka home folder hai. tmpdir() temporary folder hai. cpus() har CPU ka model aur speed deta hai. freemem() aur totalmem() bytes mein hain. uptime() boot ke baad ke seconds hain. networkInterfaces() addresses list karta hai.
Output: Windows par platform() win32 print karta hai. macOS par darwin. Linux par linux. arch() aksar x64 ya arm64 hota hai.

lessons.title: url: parse and build URLs
english: The modern API is the global URL class and URLSearchParams. You do not need to import them. The old url.parse, url.format, and url.resolve still exist on "node:url", but new code should use URL.

URL properties: href is the whole string. origin is protocol plus host. protocol includes the colon, such as https:. username and password come from the userinfo part. host includes the port. hostname does not. port is a string. pathname is the path. search includes the question mark. searchParams is a URLSearchParams object. hash includes the #.

URL methods: the constructor new URL(input, base) parses a string. If input is relative, base fills in the missing origin. toString and toJSON return href. canParse(input, base) returns true or false without throwing. URL.revokeObjectURL and URL.createObjectURL are browser APIs and are not the Node tools you want here.

Helpers from "node:url": pathToFileURL turns a file path into a file: URL. fileURLToPath does the reverse. domainToASCII and domainToUnicode convert international domain names. urlToHttpOptions turns a URL into the options object used by http.request.
URLSearchParams methods: get, getAll, has, set, append, delete, sort, keys, values, entries, forEach, toString. toString does not include the leading question mark.
Output: for https://example.com:443/docs?q=node#top, hostname prints example.com, pathname prints /docs, searchParams.get("q") prints node, and hash prints #top.
hindi: Modern API global URL class aur URLSearchParams hai. Import zaroori nahi. Purane url.parse ko naye code mein avoid karo.

Properties: href poora string hai. protocol colon ke saath hota hai, jaise https:. hostname port ke bina hota hai. host port ke saath. pathname path hai. search question mark ke saath hai. hash # ke saath hai.
new URL(input, base) string parse karta hai. canParse true ya false deta hai, throw nahi karta. pathToFileURL file path ko file: URL banata hai. fileURLToPath ulta karta hai.
URLSearchParams methods: get, getAll, has, set, append, delete, sort, toString. toString question mark nahi lagata.
Output: hostname example.com hai, pathname /docs hai, q ki value node hai, aur hash #top hai.

lessons.title: util: helpers
english: Import it with import util from "node:util". It is a toolbox. It is not a replacement for your own functions.

Methods: format(template, ...args) works like printf. %s is a string, %d is a number, %j is JSON, and %% is a percent sign. inspect(value, options) makes a debug string. colors, depth, and showHidden are useful options. isDeepStrictEqual(a, b) compares values the way assert.deepStrictEqual does. promisify(fn) turns an error-first callback function into a function that returns a promise. callbackify does the reverse. deprecate(fn, message) wraps a function so the first call warns. debuglog(section) returns a logger that prints only when NODE_DEBUG includes that section. parseArgs(config) reads process.argv into values and positionals. stripVTControlCharacters removes color codes. styleText(style, text) adds terminal color. types.isPromise, types.isDate, types.isNativeError, and the other types.is checks identify boxed and built-in objects. getSystemErrorName(code) turns a numeric errno into a name such as ENOENT.
Output: util.format("id=%d", 3) prints id=3. util.isDeepStrictEqual({ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }) prints true.
hindi: Import util from "node:util" se import karo. Ye helper toolbox hai.

Methods: format printf ki tarah kaam karta hai. %s string hai, %d number hai, %j JSON hai. inspect debug string banata hai. promisify error-first callback ko promise function bana deta hai. callbackify ulta karta hai. parseArgs process.argv padhta hai. types.isPromise jaise checks object ka type batate hain.
Output: format("id=%d", 3) id=3 print karta hai. isDeepStrictEqual true print karta hai jab dono objects same hon.

lessons.title: crypto: hashes and random bytes
english: Import it with import crypto from "node:crypto". Use it for hashes, random values, HMAC, passwords, and signatures. Do not invent your own cipher.

Hash and HMAC: createHash(algorithm) then update(data) then digest(encoding). getHashes() lists names such as sha256 and sha512. createHmac(algorithm, key) is a hash that also uses a secret. digest encodings are hex, base64, and base64url.

Random methods: randomBytes(size) returns a buffer. randomUUID() returns an RFC 4122 id. randomInt(min, max) returns an integer, and max is excluded. randomFill and randomFillSync fill an existing buffer.

Keys and ciphers: generateKeyPair and generateKeyPairSync make key pairs. publicEncrypt and privateDecrypt use them. createCipheriv and createDecipheriv encrypt with a key and an initialization vector. createSign and createVerify sign and check a signature. pbkdf2, pbkdf2Sync, scrypt, and scryptSync turn a password into a key. timingSafeEqual compares two buffers without leaking timing. Do not compare secrets with ===.
Output: sha256 of the text hello, as hex, is 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824. randomUUID() changes every call, so there is no single correct string.
hindi: Import crypto from "node:crypto" se import karo. Hashes, random values, HMAC, passwords, aur signatures ke liye use karo. Apna cipher mat banao.

createHash algorithm leta hai, update data leta hai, digest encoding mein result deta hai. createHmac secret key ke saath hash hai. randomBytes buffer deta hai. randomUUID id deta hai. randomInt integer deta hai. createCipheriv encrypt karta hai. pbkdf2 password se key banata hai. timingSafeEqual secrets compare karta hai. Secrets ko === se mat compare karo.
Output: hello ka sha256 hex 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824 hai. randomUUID har call par badalta hai.

lessons.title: zlib: compress and decompress
english: Import it with import zlib from "node:zlib". Sync methods end in Sync and return a buffer. The same names without Sync take a callback. Wrap those with util.promisify when you want a promise.

Sync and callback methods: gzipSync and gzip compress with gzip. gunzipSync and gunzip undo it. deflateSync and inflateSync use the raw deflate format. brotliCompressSync and brotliDecompressSync use Brotli. unzipSync accepts either gzip or deflate. The stream factories are createGzip, createGunzip, createDeflate, createInflate, createBrotliCompress, and createBrotliDecompress. constants holds flush and level values such as Z_BEST_COMPRESSION.
Output: gzipSync of the text hello returns a buffer whose first bytes are the gzip header 1f8b. gunzipSync of that buffer returns hello.
hindi: Import zlib from "node:zlib" se import karo. gzipSync compress karta hai. gunzipSync wapas text banata hai. deflateSync aur inflateSync deflate format hain. brotliCompressSync Brotli use karta hai. createGzip stream factory hai.
Output: hello ka gzip buffer 1f8b se shuru hota hai. gunzipSync us buffer se hello wapas deta hai.

lessons.title: dns: look up host names
english: Import the promise API with import dns from "node:dns/promises". The callback API is import dns from "node:dns". A lookup uses the operating system resolver, the same idea as getaddrinfo. resolve asks a DNS server for a specific record and does not use the hosts file the same way.

Methods: lookup(hostname) returns an address and family, 4 or 6. lookupService(address, port) reverses that to a host name and service. resolve(hostname, rrtype) returns records. resolve4 and resolve6 return A and AAAA addresses. resolveMx returns mail servers. resolveTxt returns text records. resolveCname, resolveNs, resolveSrv, resolvePtr, resolveSoa, resolveCaa, and resolveNaptr read those record types. resolveAny returns mixed records. reverse(ip) finds host names for an address. setServers and getServers change the DNS servers for resolve, not for lookup. setDefaultResultOrder("ipv4first" or "verbatim") changes lookup order.
Output: lookup("localhost") usually prints 127.0.0.1 and family 4. A public name such as example.com can change, so do not hard-code that address in a test.
hindi: Promise API node:dns/promises hai. lookup operating system resolver use karta hai. resolve DNS server se ek record type maangta hai.

Methods: lookup address aur family deta hai. resolve4 A records deta hai. resolve6 AAAA records. resolveMx mail servers. resolveTxt text records. reverse IP se host name dhoondhta hai. setServers DNS servers badalta hai.
Output: lookup("localhost") aksar 127.0.0.1 aur family 4 deta hai.

lessons.title: net: TCP sockets
english: Import it with import net from "node:net". This is TCP, not HTTP. HTTP is built on top of it. Use net when you speak a custom protocol or you want a raw socket.

Methods: createServer(connectionListener) makes a server. server.listen(port) starts it. server.close stops new connections. server.address() returns the bound port and address. createConnection(options) and connect(port, host) open a client socket. isIP(input) returns 0, 4, or 6. isIPv4 and isIPv6 return booleans. BlockList checks whether an address is blocked.

Socket methods: write(data) sends bytes and returns false when the kernel buffer is full. end() half-closes the write side. destroy() drops the socket. pause, resume, and the data event work because a socket is a Duplex stream. setTimeout, setKeepAlive, setNoDelay, and setEncoding tune the socket. remoteAddress and localPort describe the connection.
Output: isIP("127.0.0.1") prints 4. isIP("::1") prints 6. isIP("hello") prints 0. A server that writes pong and ends will make the client print pong.
hindi: Import net from "node:net" se import karo. Ye TCP hai, HTTP nahi. HTTP isi ke upar banta hai.

Methods: createServer server banata hai. listen port par sunta hai. close naye connections rokta hai. createConnection client socket kholta hai. isIP 0, 4, ya 6 deta hai. Socket write bytes bhejta hai. end write side band karta hai. destroy socket gira deta hai.
Output: isIP("127.0.0.1") 4 print karta hai. isIP("::1") 6 print karta hai. isIP("hello") 0 print karta hai.

lessons.title: readline: line by line input
english: Import it with import readline from "node:readline", or readline from "node:readline/promises" when you want question() to return a promise. It reads a stream one line at a time. The usual stream is process.stdin.

Methods: createInterface({ input, output, prompt }) builds the interface. question(query) asks and waits for one line. setPrompt and prompt show a prompt. on("line", listener) fires for every line, without the trailing newline. on("close") fires after close(). close() stops reading. [Symbol.asyncIterator] lets you write for await (const line of rl). cursorTo, moveCursor, and clearLine from "node:readline" move the terminal cursor. emitKeypressEvents(stream) turns key presses into keypress events when the terminal is in raw mode.
Output: if the user types Ada and presses Enter, question("Name: ") resolves to the string Ada, without the newline.
hindi: Promise version node:readline/promises hai. Ye stream ko line by line padhta hai. Aksar stream process.stdin hoti hai.

Methods: createInterface interface banata hai. question ek line ka intezar karta hai. on("line") har line par chalta hai. close padhna band karta hai. clearLine aur cursorTo terminal cursor chalati hain.
Output: user Ada likh kar Enter dabaye to question ka result Ada hota hai, newline ke bina.

lessons.title: assert: check what you expect
english: Import the strict set with import assert from "node:assert/strict". The loose import from "node:assert" uses == in a few old methods. Prefer strict so 1 and "1" are not treated as equal.

Methods: ok(value) throws if value is falsy. equal(actual, expected) uses Object.is. notEqual is the opposite. deepEqual and deepStrictEqual compare object trees. notDeepEqual and notDeepStrictEqual are the opposites. strictEqual is the same idea as equal on the strict import. throws(fn, error) expects a function to throw. doesNotThrow expects silence. rejects(fn) and doesNotReject expect a promise. match and doesNotMatch test a string against a regular expression. ifError(value) throws when value is an error. fail(message) always throws. AssertionError is the error class.
Output: equal(1, "1") throws AssertionError because the types differ. equal(2 + 2, 4) prints nothing and the next line runs. A thrown assert stops the script unless you catch it.
hindi: Strict set node:assert/strict se import karo. Isme 1 aur "1" equal nahi maane jaate.

Methods: ok falsy par throw karta hai. equal Object.is use karta hai. deepEqual objects compare karta hai. throws expect karta hai ki function throw kare. rejects promise ke liye hai. match regex check karta hai. fail hamesha throw karta hai.
Output: equal(1, "1") AssertionError throw karta hai. equal(2 + 2, 4) kuch print nahi karta aur agla line chalta hai.

lessons.title: querystring: old query parser
english: Import it with import querystring from "node:querystring". It parses and builds URL query strings. New code should prefer URLSearchParams. This module remains because older tutorials and packages still call it.

Methods: parse(str, sep, eq, options) turns a=1&b=2 into an object. stringify(obj, sep, eq) does the reverse. escape and unescape encode and decode a component. The default separator is & and the default assignment character is =.
Output: parse("a=1&b=2") prints { a: "1", b: "2" }. Notice the values are strings, not numbers. stringify({ a: 1, b: 2 }) prints a=1&b=2.
hindi: Import querystring from "node:querystring" se import karo. Naye code mein URLSearchParams behtar hai. Ye module purane code ke liye ab bhi hai.
Methods: parse string ko object banata hai. stringify object ko query string banata hai. escape aur unescape component encode aur decode karte hain.
Output: parse("a=1&b=2") { a: "1", b: "2" } print karta hai. Values strings hain, numbers nahi. stringify a=1&b=2 print karta hai.

lessons.title: https: TLS requests and servers
english: Import it with import https from "node:https". It is the http module plus TLS. The request and response objects are the same shapes you already use with http. Prefer global fetch for a simple client. Use https when you need a custom agent, client certificate, or a TLS server.

Methods: get(url, callback) performs GET and calls you with the response. request(url, options, callback) starts any method. You must call req.end() after request, or the body is never sent. createServer(options, listener) starts a TLS server. options.key and options.cert are the private key and certificate. Agent and globalAgent pool sockets. request methods on the client are write, end, abort, setTimeout, getHeader, setHeader, and removeHeader.
Output: https.get of a URL prints the status code, such as 200, when the response headers arrive. The body still has to be read from the response stream.
hindi: Import https from "node:https" se import karo. Ye http plus TLS hai. Simple client ke liye fetch aasaan hai. https tab use karo jab custom agent, client certificate, ya TLS server chahiye.

Methods: get GET karta hai. request koi bhi method start karta hai. request ke baad end() call karna zaroori hai. createServer TLS server start karta hai. options.key aur options.cert key aur certificate hain.
Output: https.get status code print karta hai, jaise 200, jab headers aa jaate hain. Body response stream se padhni padti hai.

lessons.title: string_decoder: split multibyte characters
english: Import it with import { StringDecoder } from "node:string_decoder". A TCP chunk or file chunk can split a multibyte character in half. If you call buffer.toString on each chunk, that character becomes garbage. StringDecoder keeps the incomplete bytes until the next chunk.

Methods: new StringDecoder(encoding) creates the decoder. The default encoding is utf8. write(buffer) returns the complete characters and holds a partial character back. end() flushes what remains, so call it when the stream closes. There is no other method. The class is small on purpose.
Output: writing the euro sign € as utf8 takes three bytes, 0xe2 0x82 0xac. write of only the first two bytes prints an empty string. write of the last byte, or end(), then prints €.
hindi: Import { StringDecoder } from "node:string_decoder" se import karo. Ek chunk multibyte character ko beech mein kaat sakta hai. Har chunk par toString garbage bana sakta hai. StringDecoder adhoore bytes agle chunk tak rakhta hai.
Methods: new StringDecoder(encoding) decoder banata hai. write poore characters deta hai aur adhoora character rok kar rakhta hai. end bacha hua flush karta hai. Aur koi method nahi hai.
Output: euro sign ke pehle do bytes par write khaali string deta hai. Aakhri byte ya end() € print karta hai.

lessons.title: tty: is this a terminal
english: Import it with import tty from "node:tty". It detects and controls a terminal. process.stdin and process.stdout are tty streams when you run the program in a terminal, and plain pipes when you redirect them to a file.

Methods: isatty(fd) returns true when a file descriptor is a terminal. ReadStream.prototype.setRawMode(true) sends key presses immediately instead of waiting for Enter. WriteStream.prototype.clearLine(dir), cursorTo(x, y), moveCursor(dx, dy), getWindowSize(), hasColors(), getColorDepth(), and clearScreenDown control the screen. columns and rows are the current size. The resize event fires when the window changes.
Output: tty.isatty(1) prints true when you run node in a terminal, because fd 1 is stdout. It prints false when you run node app.js > out.txt, because stdout is a file.
hindi: Import tty from "node:tty" se import karo. Ye batata hai ki stream terminal hai ya nahi. Output file mein bhejne par stdout terminal nahi rehta.
Methods: isatty(fd) true deta hai jab descriptor terminal ho. setRawMode key presses turant bhejta hai. clearLine, cursorTo, aur moveCursor screen control karte hain. columns aur rows size hain.
Output: terminal mein tty.isatty(1) true hota hai. node app.js > out.txt par ye false hota hai.

lessons.title: A small HTTP server
english: The built-in http module can listen on a port and send a response. You do not need a framework to understand the request and response cycle.
createServer receives a request and a response. You set a status, a content type, and the body, then end the response. listen starts the server.
Frameworks such as Express sit on top of this idea and add routing, JSON helpers, and middleware.
hindi: Built-in http module ek port par sun sakta hai aur response bhej sakta hai. Request aur response cycle samajhne ke liye framework zaroori nahi.
createServer ko request aur response milte hain. Aap status, content type, aur body set karke response end karte ho. listen server start karta hai.
Express jaisa framework isi idea ke upar routing, JSON helpers, aur middleware jodta hai.

lessons.title: Request method and URL
english: The request object tells you the HTTP method and the URL. req.method is GET or POST. req.url is the path plus the query string, not just a clean pathname.
Branch on the method and path before you write the response. Unknown paths should answer 404. Always end the response, or the browser waits forever.
hindi: Request object HTTP method aur URL batata hai. req.method GET ya POST hota hai. req.url path aur query string hai, sirf saaf pathname nahi.
Response likhne se pehle method aur path par branch karo. Anjaan path par 404 bhejo. Response hamesha end karo, warna browser intezar karta rehta hai.

lessons.title: Reading a JSON body
english: The request body arrives as a stream of chunks. Collect the chunks, join them, and JSON.parse the string. A bad body should get status 400, not a crash.
Limit the size you accept. An unbounded body can exhaust memory. Frameworks do this for you. If you use the raw http module, you must do it yourself.
hindi: Request body chunks ki stream mein aati hai. Chunks jodo, string banao, aur JSON.parse karo. Galat body par status 400 do, crash mat hone do.
Jo size accept karte ho, use limit karo. Bina limit ke body memory khatam kar sakti hai. Frameworks ye khud karte hain. Raw http module mein ye aapko karna padta hai.

lessons.title: Why Express exists
english: Express is a small layer on Node's http server. It gives you routes, a request body parser, and a chain of functions called middleware. You install it with npm install express.
The same ideas exist in newer frameworks such as Fastify. Learn Express first if most tutorials around you use it. The mental model of request, middleware, and response stays useful either way.
hindi: Express Node ke http server par ek chhoti layer hai. Ye routes, request body parser, aur middleware naam ki functions ki chain deta hai. npm install express se install hota hai.
Yahi ideas naye frameworks mein bhi hain, jaise Fastify. Agar aas-paas ke tutorials Express use karte hain to pehle Express seekho. Request, middleware, aur response ka model dono mein kaam aata hai.

lessons.title: Routes and parameters
english: A route matches a method and a path. app.get handles GET. app.post handles POST. A path segment that starts with a colon, such as /users/:id, is a parameter. Read it from req.params.id.
Query strings live on req.query. A request to /search?q=node sets req.query.q to node. Keep route handlers small and move shared checks into middleware.
hindi: Route method aur path match karta hai. app.get GET handle karta hai. app.post POST handle karta hai. Colon se shuru segment, jaise /users/:id, parameter hai. Use req.params.id se padho.
Query strings req.query par hoti hain. /search?q=node par req.query.q node hota hai. Route handlers chhote rakho aur shared checks middleware mein rakho.

lessons.title: Middleware
english: Middleware is a function that runs before the route handler. It receives req, res, and next. Call next to continue. If you do not call next or send a response, the request hangs.
express.json() is built-in middleware that parses a JSON body onto req.body. Your own middleware can check a header, log the path, or stop the request with a status code.
hindi: Middleware woh function hai jo route handler se pehle chalta hai. Use req, res, aur next milte hain. Aage badhne ke liye next call karo. next na call karo aur response bhi na bhejo to request atki rehti hai.
express.json() built-in middleware hai jo JSON body ko req.body par rakhta hai. Apna middleware header check kar sakta hai, path log kar sakta hai, ya status code ke saath request rok sakta hai.

lessons.title: Error-handling middleware
english: An error middleware has four arguments: error, req, res, and next. Express only treats it as an error handler because of that extra argument. Register it after your routes.
In async routes, a rejected promise is not caught unless you pass it to next or use a wrapper. Call next(error) so the error middleware can send one JSON error instead of crashing.
hindi: Error middleware ke char arguments hote hain: error, req, res, aur next. Express use error handler isliye maanta hai kyunki ek extra argument hai. Ise routes ke baad register karo.
Async routes mein rejected promise tab tak nahi pakdi jati jab tak use next na do ya wrapper use na karo. next(error) call karo taaki error middleware ek JSON error bheje, crash na ho.

lessons.title: REST shape
english: A REST API uses URLs for resources and HTTP methods for actions. GET reads. POST creates. PUT or PATCH updates. DELETE removes. The status code tells the client what happened.
201 means created. 400 means the client sent a bad body. 404 means the resource is missing. 500 means the server failed. Send JSON with a clear shape and do not leak stack traces to clients.
hindi: REST API resources ke liye URLs aur actions ke liye HTTP methods use karti hai. GET padhta hai. POST banata hai. PUT ya PATCH update karta hai. DELETE hataata hai. Status code batata hai kya hua.
201 ka matlab created. 400 ka matlab client ne galat body bheji. 404 ka matlab resource nahi mila. 500 ka matlab server fail hua. Saaf JSON bhejo aur clients ko stack trace mat do.

lessons.title: Environment variables
english: Secrets and ports belong in the environment, not in source code. Read them from process.env. A missing required variable should stop startup with a clear message.
Locally, people often load a .env file with a package such as dotenv. Do not commit real secrets. Commit an example file that lists the names without the values.
hindi: Secrets aur ports environment mein hone chahiye, source code mein nahi. Unhe process.env se padho. Zaroori variable missing ho to startup saaf message ke saath ruk jaye.
Local par log aksar dotenv jaise package se .env file load karte hain. Asli secrets commit mat karo. Example file commit karo jisme sirf naam hon, values na hon.

lessons.title: Calling another API
english: Modern Node includes fetch. It returns a promise. Check response.ok before you parse JSON. A 404 still resolves the promise. ok is false when the status is not in the 200 range.
Set a timeout or abort the request if the other service is slow. Do not let one hung call hold a request handler open with no limit.
hindi: Modern Node mein fetch shamil hai. Ye promise return karta hai. JSON parse karne se pehle response.ok check karo. 404 par bhi promise resolve hota hai. Status 200 range mein na ho to ok false hota hai.
Doosri service slow ho to timeout lagao ya request abort karo. Ek atki hui call ko bina limit ke request handler pakde mat rehne do.

lessons.title: Child processes
english: child_process starts another program. exec runs a shell command and buffers the output. spawn streams the output and does not invoke a shell unless you ask. Prefer spawn when you pass user input, so the shell cannot reinterpret it.
A child has its own memory. Use it for a tool such as a compiler. Do not start unlimited children. Wait for the close event and handle a non-zero exit code.
hindi: child_process doosra program start karta hai. exec shell command chalata hai aur output buffer karta hai. spawn output stream karta hai aur shell tabhi chalata hai jab aap kahen. User input par spawn prefer karo, taaki shell use dobara na padhe.
Child ki apni memory hoti hai. Compiler jaise tool ke liye use karo. Unlimited children mat kholo. close event ka intezar karo aur non-zero exit code handle karo.

lessons.title: Cluster
english: Node's JavaScript runs on one thread per process. The cluster module forks several processes that share the same server port. The operating system spreads connections across them.
Workers do not share memory. A value set in one worker is invisible to the others. For shared state, use a database or a store such as Redis. If a worker dies, the primary can fork a replacement.
hindi: Node ka JavaScript har process mein ek thread par chalta hai. cluster module kai processes fork karta hai jo ek hi server port share karte hain. Operating system connections un par baantta hai.
Workers memory share nahi karte. Ek worker ki value doosre ko nahi dikhti. Shared state ke liye database ya Redis jaisa store use karo. Worker mar jaye to primary naya fork kar sakta hai.

lessons.title: How to use Cluster
english: Cluster module forks multiple processes that share the same server port. Each worker runs on its own thread and does not share memory with others, so shared state must go to a database or Redis. If a worker dies, the primary process can fork a replacement. Example: const cluster=require('cluster'); if(cluster.isMaster){ for(let i=0;i<4;i++) cluster.fork(); } else { require('http').createServer((req,res)=>res.end('Hello')).listen(8000); }
hindi: Cluster module forks multiple processes that share the same server port. Each worker runs on its own thread and does not share memory with others, so shared state must go to a database or Redis. If a worker dies, the primary process can fork a replacement. Example: const cluster=require('cluster'); if(cluster.isMaster){ for(let i=0;i<4;i++) cluster.fork(); } else { require('http').createServer((req,res)=>res.end('Hello')).listen(8000); }

lessons.title: Worker threads
english: worker_threads run JavaScript on another thread inside the same process. Use them for CPU work such as image processing or heavy parsing. They are not required for normal database or HTTP waiting. The event loop already handles that.
Threads talk by posting messages. They do not share your objects unless you use shared memory on purpose. Keep the worker's job small and well defined.
hindi: worker_threads ek hi process ke andar doosre thread par JavaScript chalate hain. Inhe CPU kaam ke liye use karo, jaise image processing ya bhari parsing. Normal database ya HTTP wait ke liye ye zaroori nahi. Event loop woh pehle se karta hai.
Threads messages bhejkar baat karte hain. Jab tak aap jaan kar shared memory na use karo, objects share nahi hote. Worker ka kaam chhota aur clear rakho.

lessons.title: WebSockets
english: HTTP is a request and a response. A WebSocket stays open so the server can push messages. Chat, live scores, and dashboards use it. Socket.IO is a popular library that adds rooms and a fallback when WebSocket is blocked.
One Node process holds those connections in memory. Several processes need a shared adapter, often Redis, so a message published on one process reaches sockets on the others.
hindi: HTTP ek request aur ek response hai. WebSocket khula rehta hai taaki server messages push kar sake. Chat, live scores, aur dashboards ise use karte hain. Socket.IO popular library hai jo rooms aur fallback jodti hai jab WebSocket block ho.
Ek Node process un connections ko memory mein rakhta hai. Kai processes ko shared adapter chahiye, aksar Redis, taaki ek process ka message doosri process ke sockets tak pahunche.

lessons.title: How to use WebSockets
english: A WebSocket stays open, so the server can push a message whenever it wants. Chat, live scores, and dashboards use that. You need a small Node server and a page that connects to it.
Install the ws package and listen on a port. When a browser connects, send a welcome message. When a message arrives, print it and send an echo back.
In the browser, open ws://localhost:8080. After the connection opens, send Hello server. When the server replies, print e.data.
Socket.IO is the same idea with a shorter API. It adds rooms and a fallback when a plain WebSocket is blocked. The server emits an event, and every client can listen for it.
hindi: WebSocket khula rehta hai, isliye server jab chahe message bhej sakta hai. Chat, live scores, aur dashboards isi liye ise use karte hain. Ek chhota Node server chahiye aur ek page jo usse jude.
ws package install karke ek port par suno. Browser connect ho to welcome bhejo. Message aaye to use print karo aur echo wapas bhejo.
Browser mein ws://localhost:8080 kholo. Connection khulne ke baad Hello server bhejo. Server jawab de to e.data print karo.
Socket.IO wahi kaam chhote API se karta hai. Ye rooms jodta hai aur fallback deta hai jab seedha WebSocket block ho. Server event emit karta hai aur har client sun sakta hai.

title: JavaScript
summary: Values, functions, arrays, and asynchronous code.

lessons.title: Values and variables
english: A variable is a name for a value. Use const when the binding will not be reassigned, and let when it will. Avoid var in new code.
JavaScript types include string, number, boolean, null, undefined, object, and symbol. Arrays and functions are objects with special behavior.
=== compares value and type. == converts types first, which hides bugs. Prefer ===.
hindi: Variable ek value ka naam hai. const tab use karo jab binding badlegi nahi, aur let tab jab badlegi. Naye code mein var avoid karo.
JavaScript types mein string, number, boolean, null, undefined, object, aur symbol aate hain. Array aur function bhi object hain, lekin unka behavior khaas hota hai.
=== value aur type dono compare karta hai. == pehle type convert karta hai, isliye bugs chhup sakte hain. === behtar hai.

lessons.title: Functions and arrays
english: A function is a reusable block. Parameters are the inputs. The return value is what the caller receives. If you forget return, the result is undefined.
Arrow functions are a short form. They are handy for callbacks. A method that uses this should usually stay a regular function.
Arrays hold ordered values. map builds a new array, filter keeps matching items, and find returns the first match.
hindi: Function ek dobara use hone wala block hai. Parameters input hain. return wahi value hai jo caller ko milti hai. return bhool gaye to result undefined hota hai.
Arrow function chhota form hai. Callbacks ke liye ye aasaan hai. Jo method this use karta hai, use aksar normal function hi rehna chahiye.
Array ordered values rakhta hai. map naya array banata hai, filter matching items rakhta hai, aur find pehla match deta hai.

lessons.title: Promises and async
english: A promise represents work that finishes later. It can succeed with a value or fail with an error. then handles success. catch handles failure.
async and await let you write that flow like normal steps. await pauses that function until the promise settles. The rest of the program keeps running.
Wrap awaited calls in try and catch when failure is possible, such as a network request.
hindi: Promise aisa kaam dikhata hai jo baad mein khatam hota hai. Ye value ke saath succeed ho sakta hai ya error ke saath fail. then success handle karta hai. catch failure handle karta hai.
async aur await se ye flow normal steps jaisa likha jata hai. await us function ko rokta hai jab tak promise settle na ho. Baaki program chalta rehta hai.
Jahan failure ho sakti hai, jaise network request, wahan awaited call ko try aur catch mein rakho.

lessons.title: Sample text
english: The string lessons use the text JavaScript and the padded text '  Hello Ada  '. A string is a list of characters. The first index is 0. length is a property, not a method, and it counts characters.
Output: 'JavaScript'.length is 10.
hindi: String lessons JavaScript aur '  Hello Ada  ' text use karte hain. String characters ki list hai. Pehla index 0 hai. length property hai, method nahi, aur characters ginti hai.
Output: length 10 hai.

lessons.title: charAt, at, and charCodeAt
english: charAt(index) returns the character at that index. at(index) does the same and also accepts a negative index, where -1 is the last character. charCodeAt(index) returns the UTF-16 code of that character. codePointAt(index) returns the full Unicode code point.
Output: charAt(0) is J. at(-1) is t. charCodeAt(0) is 74, the code for J.
hindi: charAt index par character deta hai. at bhi wahi karta hai aur negative index leta hai, -1 aakhri character hai. charCodeAt us character ka UTF-16 code deta hai.
Output: charAt(0) J hai. at(-1) t hai. charCodeAt(0) 74 hai.

lessons.title: slice, substring, and concat
english: slice(start, end) returns the part from start up to, but not including, end. A negative start counts from the end. substring(start, end) is similar but treats a negative index as 0. concat joins strings. The + operator does the same job and is the usual choice.
Output: slice(0, 4) is Java. slice(-6) is Script. concat(' and ', 'types') is JavaScript and types.
hindi: slice start se end se pehle tak ka hissa deta hai. Negative start end se ginta hai. substring negative index ko 0 maanta hai. concat strings jodta hai. + operator bhi yahi karta hai.
Output: slice(0, 4) Java hai. slice(-6) Script hai.

lessons.title: indexOf, includes, startsWith, and endsWith
english: indexOf(text) returns the first index, or -1 when the text is missing. lastIndexOf returns the last index. includes returns true or false. startsWith and endsWith check the beginning and the end. You can pass a start index to indexOf, includes, and startsWith.
Output: indexOf('Script') is 4. includes('Java') is true. startsWith('Java') is true. endsWith('script') is false because the match is case sensitive.
hindi: indexOf pehla index deta hai, na mile to -1. lastIndexOf aakhri index deta hai. includes true ya false deta hai. startsWith shuruat check karta hai. endsWith end check karta hai. Ye case sensitive hain.
Output: indexOf('Script') 4 hai. endsWith('script') false hai kyunki S capital hai.

lessons.title: replace, split, and match
english: replace(search, next) changes the first match. replaceAll changes every match. split(separator) turns a string into an array. match(regex) returns the matches. search(regex) returns the index of the first match, or -1.
Output: replace('Java', 'Type') is TypeScript. 'a-b-a'.replaceAll('a', 'c') is c-b-c. 'Ada,Grace'.split(',') is ['Ada', 'Grace'].
hindi: replace pehla match badalta hai. replaceAll har match badalta hai. split string ko array banata hai. match regex ke matches deta hai. search pehle match ka index deta hai.
Output: replace se TypeScript milta hai. replaceAll se c-b-c milta hai. split se ['Ada', 'Grace'] milta hai.

lessons.title: case, trim, pad, and repeat
english: toLowerCase and toUpperCase change case. trim removes spaces from both ends. trimStart and trimEnd remove spaces from one end. padStart(length, fill) and padEnd add characters until the string reaches that length. repeat(count) copies the string.
Output: 'JavaScript'.toLowerCase() is javascript. '  Hello Ada  '.trim() is Hello Ada. '5'.padStart(3, '0') is 005. 'ha'.repeat(3) is hahaha.
hindi: toLowerCase aur toUpperCase case badalte hain. trim dono taraf se space hataata hai. trimStart aur trimEnd ek taraf se hataate hain. padStart aur padEnd length poori karte hain. repeat string ko dohrata hai.
Output: toLowerCase javascript deta hai. trim Hello Ada deta hai. padStart 005 deta hai. repeat hahaha deta hai.

lessons.title: Sample numbers
english: The array lessons use scores = [10, 20, 30] unless a lesson says otherwise. An array keeps order. Index 0 is 10. length is 3. Arrays are objects, so you can add methods, but the built-in methods below are the ones you use every day.
Output: scores[0] is 10 and scores.length is 3.
hindi: Array lessons scores = [10, 20, 30] use karte hain, jab tak lesson kuch aur na kahe. Array order rakhta hai. Index 0 par 10 hai. length 3 hai.
Output: pehla item 10 hai aur length 3 hai.

lessons.title: push, pop, shift, and unshift
english: push adds items at the end and returns the new length. pop removes the last item and returns it. unshift adds items at the start and returns the new length. shift removes the first item and returns it. These four change the original array.
Output: start from [10, 20, 30]. push(40) returns 4 and the array is [10, 20, 30, 40]. pop() returns 40. shift() returns 10.
hindi: push end mein jodta hai aur nayi length deta hai. pop aakhri item hata kar use deta hai. unshift shuru mein jodta hai. shift pehla item hata kar use deta hai. Ye chaaron original array badalte hain.
Output: push(40) length 4 deta hai. pop 40 deta hai. shift 10 deta hai.

lessons.title: slice, splice, and concat
english: slice(start, end) copies a part and does not change the original. splice(start, deleteCount, ...items) changes the original: it removes items and can insert new ones. concat returns a new array joined with other values. toSpliced is the copy form of splice and leaves the original alone.
hindi: slice hissa copy karta hai aur original nahi badalta. splice original badalta hai: items hataata hai aur naye laga sakta hai. concat naya joda hua array deta hai.
Output: slice(1) [20, 30] hai. splice ke baad [10, 25, 30] rehta hai.

lessons.title: find, includes, and indexOf
english: indexOf(value) and lastIndexOf(value) search with === and return an index or -1. includes(value) returns true or false. find(fn) returns the first item for which fn returns true, or undefined. findIndex returns that index, or -1. findLast and findLastIndex start from the end.
Output: [10, 20, 30].includes(20) is true. find of a score greater than 15 is 20. indexOf(30) is 2. find of a score greater than 100 is undefined.
hindi: indexOf aur lastIndexOf === se dhoondhte hain aur index ya -1 dete hain. includes true ya false deta hai. find pehla item deta hai jise function true kahe, warna undefined. findIndex uska index deta hai.
Output: includes(20) true hai. 15 se bada pehla score 20 hai. indexOf(30) 2 hai.

lessons.title: map, filter, reduce, some, and every
english: map builds a new array by running a function on each item. filter keeps the items for which the function returns true. reduce folds the array into one value. forEach runs a function and returns undefined. some returns true when any item passes. every returns true only when all items pass.
Output: [10, 20, 30].map(n => n * 2) is [20, 40, 60]. filter(n => n > 15) is [20, 30]. reduce to a sum is 60. some(n => n > 25) is true. every(n => n > 25) is false.
hindi: map har item par function chala kar naya array banata hai. filter woh items rakhta hai jinke liye function true de. reduce poori array ko ek value bana deta hai. some tab true hai jab koi ek item pass kare. every tab true hai jab sab pass karen.
Output: map [20, 40, 60] deta hai. filter [20, 30] deta hai. sum 60 hai. some true hai. every false hai.

lessons.title: sort, reverse, join, and flat
english: sort() changes the original and sorts as text unless you pass a compare function. For numbers, use (a, b) => a - b. toSorted returns a new array. reverse and toReversed flip the order. join(separator) makes one string. flat(depth) opens nested arrays. flatMap maps and then flats one level.
hindi: sort original badalta hai aur bina compare function ke text ki tarah sort karta hai. Numbers ke liye (a, b) => a - b do. toSorted naya array deta hai. reverse order ulta karta hai. join ek string banata hai. flat nested arrays kholta hai.
Output: number sort [2, 10, 30] hai. join 10-20-30 hai. flat [1, 2, 3] hai.

lessons.title: toFixed, toString, and parse
english: toString(radix) turns a number into text. radix 2 is binary and 16 is hex. toFixed(digits) rounds and returns a string with that many decimal places. toPrecision(digits) sets the total significant digits. toExponential() uses scientific notation.

Number(value) converts a whole value. parseInt(text, 10) reads an integer and stops at the first bad character. parseFloat reads a decimal. Number.isNaN is true only for the NaN value. Number.isInteger is true for whole numbers. Number.isFinite rejects Infinity and NaN.
Output: (12.345).toFixed(2) is '12.35'. parseInt('08px', 10) is 8. Number.isInteger(4) is true. Number('Ada') is NaN.
hindi: toString number ko text banata hai. toFixed decimal places set karta hai aur string deta hai. toPrecision significant digits set karta hai. Number poori value convert karta hai. parseInt integer padhta hai. parseFloat decimal padhta hai. Number.isInteger whole number check karta hai.
Output: toFixed(2) '12.35' hai. parseInt('08px', 10) 8 hai. Number('Ada') NaN hai.

lessons.title: round, floor, ceil, and trunc
english: Math.round picks the nearest integer. Halves round up, so 4.5 becomes 5. Math.floor goes down to the integer. Math.ceil goes up. Math.trunc drops the fraction without rounding. Math.sign returns 1, -1, or 0. Math.abs drops the minus sign.
Output: round(4.5) is 5. floor(4.9) is 4. ceil(4.1) is 5. trunc(-4.9) is -4. abs(-7) is 7.
hindi: Math.round nazdeek integer chunta hai. 4.5 par 5 hota hai. floor neeche jata hai. ceil upar jata hai. trunc fraction hata deta hai, round kiye bina. abs minus sign hataata hai.
Output: round 5 hai. floor 4 hai. ceil 5 hai. trunc(-4.9) -4 hai. abs 7 hai.

lessons.title: pow, sqrt, min, max, and random
english: Math.pow(base, exp) raises a number. 2 ** 3 does the same. Math.sqrt returns the square root. Math.cbrt returns the cube root. Math.min and Math.max take any number of arguments. Math.random() returns a decimal from 0 up to, but not including, 1.
A dice roll from 1 to 6 is Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1. That result changes every call, so there is no single correct number.
Output: pow(2, 3) is 8. sqrt(16) is 4. max(3, 9, 1) is 9. min(3, 9, 1) is 1.
hindi: Math.pow power nikalta hai. 2 ** 3 wahi karta hai. sqrt square root hai. cbrt cube root hai. min aur max sabse chhota aur sabse bada dete hain. random 0 se 1 se pehle tak decimal deta hai.
1 se 6 ka dice Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 hai. Ye har call par badalta hai.
Output: pow 8 hai. sqrt 4 hai. max 9 hai. min 1 hai.

lessons.title: Create a date and read it
english: new Date() is the current moment. new Date('2026-10-03T00:00:00Z') parses an ISO string. Date.now() is milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. Date.parse(text) returns those milliseconds too.

getUTCFullYear, getUTCMonth, getUTCDate, getUTCDay, getUTCHours, getUTCMinutes, and getUTCSeconds read the UTC parts. getUTCMonth is 0 for January, so October is 9. getUTCDay is 0 for Sunday. The local getFullYear and getMonth follow the computer's time zone, so examples here use UTC.
Output: for 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z, the UTC year is 2026, the month is 9, and the date is 3.
hindi: new Date() abhi ka time hai. ISO string se date ban sakti hai. Date.now() 1970 se milliseconds hai. getUTCFullYear, getUTCMonth, getUTCDate UTC parts padhte hain. Month 0 January hai, isliye October 9 hai.
Output: 2026-10-03 ke liye year 2026, month 9, aur date 3 hai.

lessons.title: Set and format a date
english: setUTCFullYear, setUTCMonth, and setUTCDate change the UTC parts and return the new timestamp in milliseconds. setHours and the other local setters follow the computer's zone. toISOString() returns a UTC string. toUTCString() is a readable UTC string. toLocaleDateString(locale) formats for a language.
Output: after setUTCDate(15) on 2026-10-03, toISOString() starts with 2026-10-15.
hindi: setUTCFullYear, setUTCMonth, aur setUTCDate UTC parts badalte hain. toISOString UTC string deta hai. toLocaleDateString language ke hisaab se date dikhata hai.
Output: date 15 set karne par ISO string 2026-10-15 se shuru hoti hai.

lessons.title: keys, values, entries, and assign
english: Object.keys(obj) returns the own property names. Object.values returns the values. Object.entries returns [name, value] pairs. Object.fromEntries builds an object from those pairs. Object.assign(target, source) copies properties onto target. Object.hasOwn(obj, name) is true when the object itself has that property.

Object.freeze stops changes. Object.seal stops adding or deleting properties but still allows changing existing ones. Object.create(proto) makes an object whose prototype is proto. Object.groupBy(array, fn) groups items by the key fn returns.
Output: keys of { name: 'Ada', age: 36 } are ['name', 'age']. values are ['Ada', 36]. hasOwn(user, 'name') is true. hasOwn(user, 'toString') is false because toString comes from the prototype.
hindi: Object.keys naam deta hai. values values deti hai. entries [naam, value] pairs deti hai. fromEntries un pairs se object banata hai. assign properties copy karta hai. hasOwn khud ki property check karta hai.
freeze changes rokta hai. seal nayi property rokta hai par purani badal sakti hai. groupBy items ko key se group karta hai.
Output: keys ['name', 'age'] hain. hasOwn name par true hai aur toString par false hai.

lessons.title: parse and stringify
english: JSON.stringify(value) turns a value into a JSON string. Functions and undefined properties are dropped. Dates become ISO strings. JSON.parse(text) turns that text back into a value. A second argument to stringify can be a replacer function or a list of keys to keep. A number argument sets the indent.
Output: stringify({ name: 'Ada' }) is '{"name":"Ada"}'. parse of that text gives an object whose name is Ada. stringify of the same object with indent 2 prints the name on its own line.
hindi: JSON.stringify value ko JSON string banata hai. Functions aur undefined properties gir jaati hain. JSON.parse text ko value banata hai. Number argument indent set karta hai.
Output: stringify '{"name":"Ada"}' deta hai. parse ke baad name Ada hota hai.

lessons.title: Set methods
english: A Set stores unique values. new Set([1, 1, 2]) keeps 1 and 2. add(value) inserts a value and returns the set. has(value) returns true or false. delete(value) removes one value and returns true when it existed. clear() removes everything. size is the count. keys, values, and entries walk the set. forEach runs a function for each value.
Output: a set built from [1, 1, 2] has size 2. has(2) is true. delete(1) then has(1) is false.
hindi: Set unique values rakhta hai. add value jodta hai. has true ya false deta hai. delete hataata hai. clear sab hataata hai. size count hai.
Output: [1, 1, 2] ka size 2 hai. has(2) true hai. delete(1) ke baad has(1) false hai.

lessons.title: Map methods
english: A Map stores keys of any type, not only strings. set(key, value) adds a pair and returns the map. get(key) returns the value or undefined. has(key) checks the key. delete(key) removes one pair. clear() removes all. size is the count. keys, values, and entries walk the pairs.
Output: set('Ada', 36) then get('Ada') is 36. has('Lin') is false. size is 1 until you add another pair.
hindi: Map kisi bhi type ki key rakh sakta hai, sirf string nahi. set pair jodta hai. get value deta hai. has key check karta hai. delete pair hataata hai. size count hai.
Output: get('Ada') 36 hai. has('Lin') false hai. size 1 hai.

lessons.title: test, exec, match, and replace
english: A regular expression is written /pattern/flags. i ignores case. g finds every match. test(text) returns true or false. exec(text) returns the first match array, or null. String match, matchAll, replace, replaceAll, and search accept a regular expression.
Output: /script/i.test('JavaScript') is true. 'JavaScript'.match(/java/i)[0] is Java. 'a1b2'.match(/\d/g) is ['1', '2']. replace(/a/g, 'c') on 'a-b-a' is c-b-c.
hindi: Regular expression /pattern/flags se likhte hain. i case ignore karta hai. g har match dhoondhta hai. test true ya false deta hai. exec pehla match deta hai ya null. String ke match, replace, aur search regex lete hain.
Output: test true hai. match Java deta hai. digits ['1', '2'] hain. replace c-b-c deta hai.

title: React
summary: Build screens from components, props, and state.

lessons.title: Components and JSX
english: A React component is a function that returns UI. The name starts with a capital letter. You use it like an HTML tag.
JSX looks like HTML inside JavaScript. Curly braces insert a value. A component returns one parent, or a fragment if you do not want an extra element.
Keep components small. A page is a tree of components, each responsible for one piece of the screen.
hindi: React component ek function hai jo UI return karta hai. Naam capital letter se shuru hota hai. Use HTML tag ki tarah likhte hain.
JSX JavaScript ke andar HTML jaisa dikhta hai. Curly braces mein value daalte hain. Component ek parent return karta hai, ya fragment jab extra element nahi chahiye.
Components chhote rakho. Page components ka tree hota hai, aur har component screen ka ek hissa sambhalta hai.

lessons.title: Props and state
english: Props are inputs passed from a parent. The child should treat them as read-only. If the parent passes a new name, React renders the child again.
