Chain helpers, then await it. where(path) picks a field. equals(value) matches it. gt, gte, lt, lte, ne compare numbers and dates. in(list) and nin(list) match a list. exists(true) requires the field. regex(pattern) matches text. mod(divisor, remainder) matches a remainder. size(n) matches an array length. elemMatch(filter) matches one array element.

select('name -_id') picks fields. A minus sign excludes a field. sort({ name: 1 }) sorts ascending, -1 is descending. limit(n) and skip(n) page the results. lean() returns plain objects, which is faster when you will not call save. exec() returns the promise explicitly. cursor() streams matches one by one. populate(path) loads a related document. session(session) binds a transaction.

or([filters]) and and([filters]) and nor([filters]) combine filters. setOptions({ maxTimeMS: 1000 }) limits how long the query may run. hint(index) forces an index. collation({ locale: 'en', strength: 2 }) makes string compare case-insensitive. clone() copies the query so you can run it twice. getFilter(), getOptions(), and getQuery() read what you built.
Output: User.find().where('age').gte(18).select('name').sort({ name: 1 }).limit(2) prints at most two names, alphabetically, for users who are 18 or older.
hindi: find aur findOne Query dete hain. where field chunta hai. equals match karta hai. gt, gte, lt, lte, ne compare karte hain. in aur nin list se match karte hain. exists field maangta hai. regex text match karta hai. select fields chunta hai. sort order karta hai. limit aur skip page banate hain. lean plain object deta hai. populate related document lata hai.
or, and, aur nor filters jodte hain. setOptions maxTimeMS laga sakta hai. hint index force karta hai. clone query copy karta hai.
Output: age 18 ya usse badi ho to do naam, a se z, print hote hain.

lessons.title: Update methods
english: Model.updateOne(filter, update) changes the first match. Model.updateMany(filter, update) changes every match. Model.replaceOne(filter, replacement) replaces the whole document except _id. These return matchedCount and modifiedCount. They do not return the document.

Model.findOneAndUpdate(filter, update, options) and Model.findByIdAndUpdate(id, update, options) return a document. Without options, you get the document from before the change. Pass { new: true } to get the document after the change. { upsert: true } inserts a document when none matches. { runValidators: true } runs schema validators on the update.

Write changes with operators: $set sets fields, $unset removes one, $inc adds to a number, $push adds to an array, $pull removes array values, $addToSet adds a value only once. A plain object is treated as a replacement, not as $set, unless you wrap it.
Output: updateOne({ name: 'Ada' }, { $set: { role: 'admin' } }) prints matchedCount 1 and modifiedCount 1 when Ada exists. A second identical call prints modifiedCount 0 because nothing changed.
hindi: updateOne pehla match badalta hai. updateMany sab badalta hai. replaceOne poora document badal deta hai. Ye document nahi dete, matchedCount aur modifiedCount dete hain.

findOneAndUpdate aur findByIdAndUpdate document dete hain. { new: true } badlav ke baad wala document deta hai. { upsert: true } na mile to naya bana deta hai. { runValidators: true } validators chalata hai.
Operators: $set field set karta hai, $unset hataata hai, $inc number badhata hai, $push array mein jodta hai, $pull array se hataata hai, $addToSet ek baar jodta hai.
Output: Ada mile to matchedCount 1 aur modifiedCount 1 hota hai. Doosri same call par modifiedCount 0 hota hai.

lessons.title: Delete methods
english: Model.deleteOne(filter) deletes the first match. Model.deleteMany(filter) deletes every match. Both return deletedCount. Model.findOneAndDelete(filter) and Model.findByIdAndDelete(id) delete and return the document that was removed, or null.
doc.deleteOne() deletes that one document. The old doc.remove() and Model.remove() are deprecated. Use deleteOne or deleteMany.
Output: deleteOne({ name: 'Ada' }) prints deletedCount 1 the first time. The next findOne({ name: 'Ada' }) prints null. deleteMany({}) deletes every user and deletedCount equals how many were there.
hindi: deleteOne pehla match hataata hai. deleteMany sab hataata hai. Dono deletedCount dete hain. findOneAndDelete aur findByIdAndDelete hata kar document wapas dete hain, ya null.
doc.deleteOne() usi document ko hataata hai. Purane remove() ko use mat karo.
Output: pehli deleteOne par deletedCount 1 hota hai. Uske baad findOne null hota hai.

lessons.title: Document methods
english: doc.save() validates and writes the document. doc.validate() and doc.validateSync() check it without writing. validate returns a promise. validateSync returns an error or undefined immediately.

doc.get('name') and doc.set('name', 'Ada') read and write a path. doc.markModified('tags') tells Mongoose an array or mixed field changed. doc.isModified('name') is true after a change and before save. doc.isNew is true until the first successful save. doc.id is the string form of _id. doc.equals(other) compares ids.

doc.toObject() and doc.toJSON() return a plain object. toJSON runs when you pass the document to JSON.stringify. doc.populate(path) loads a relation on this document. doc.depopulate(path) puts the id back. doc.overwrite(obj) replaces the paths. doc.$isDeleted() is true after deleteOne.
Output: a new User has isNew true. After await user.save(), isNew is false and user.id is a 24 character hex string.
hindi: doc.save() validate karke likhta hai. doc.validate() aur doc.validateSync() bina likhe check karte hain. doc.get aur doc.set path padhte aur likhte hain. doc.markModified array change batata hai. doc.isModified batata hai path badla hai ya nahi. doc.isNew pehli save se pehle true hota hai. doc.id _id ki string hai.
doc.toObject() aur doc.toJSON() plain object dete hain. doc.populate relation lata hai. doc.depopulate id wapas laga deta hai. doc.overwrite paths replace karta hai.
Output: naya user isNew true hota hai. save ke baad isNew false hota hai aur id 24 character hex hoti hai.

lessons.title: Aggregate methods
english: Model.aggregate(pipeline) runs a MongoDB pipeline. You can also start with Model.aggregate() and chain stages. match(filter) is like find. group({ _id, total: { $sum: 1 } }) folds documents. project(fields) and addFields(fields) shape each document. sort, skip, and limit work like query helpers.

lookup({ from, localField, foreignField, as }) joins another collection. unwind(path) turns an array into one document per element. count('n') counts the rows so far. facet({ a: pipeline, b: pipeline }) runs several pipelines on the same input. replaceRoot and replaceWith make a nested object the new root. sample(n) picks random documents. exec() runs the pipeline.
Output: User.aggregate([{ $group: { _id: '$role', n: { $sum: 1 } } }]) returns one object per role. If two users are admins, one object is { _id: 'admin', n: 2 }.
hindi: Model.aggregate pipeline chalata hai. match find jaisa hai. group documents jodta hai. project aur addFields shape badalte hain. sort, skip, aur limit bhi hain.
lookup doosri collection jodta hai. unwind array ko alag documents banata hai. count rows ginta hai. facet kai pipelines ek saath chalata hai. exec pipeline chalata hai.
Output: group by role par har role ka count aata hai. Do admin hon to { _id: 'admin', n: 2 } milta hai.

lessons.title: Sample users and orders
english: The next examples use two collections. users has Ada, Grace, and Lin. orders has two purchases for Ada and one for Grace. Create them once, then run each stage on this same data.
Ada and Grace are admins. Lin is a member. Ada is 36, Grace is 45, and Lin is 28. Ada bought a book for 12 and a pen for 3. Grace bought a book for 12.
hindi: Agle examples do collections use karte hain. users mein Ada, Grace, aur Lin hain. orders mein Ada ki do kharidi aur Grace ki ek kharidi hai. Inhe ek baar banao, phir har stage isi data par chalao.
Ada aur Grace admin hain. Lin member hai. Ada 36 ki hai, Grace 45 ki, Lin 28 ki. Ada ne 12 ki book aur 3 ka pen kharida. Grace ne 12 ki book kharidi.

lessons.title: $match
english: $match keeps documents that pass a filter. It uses the same rules as find. Put it first when you can, so later stages do less work.
Use: { $match: { role: 'admin' } } keeps Ada and Grace and drops Lin. A range such as { age: { $gte: 30 } } also keeps Ada and Grace, because 36 and 45 are at least 30, and drops Lin at 28.
Output: the names are Ada and Grace. Lin is not in the array.
hindi: $match woh documents rakhta hai jo filter pass karte hain. Ye find jaisa hai. Ise shuru mein rakho taaki baad ke stages ko kam kaam mile.
Use: role admin Ada aur Grace rakhta hai, Lin hata deta hai. age 30 ya usse badi bhi Ada aur Grace rakhti hai, kyunki Lin 28 ka hai.
Output: naam Ada aur Grace hain. Lin array mein nahi hai.

lessons.title: $group
english: $group folds many documents into one per _id. _id is the value you group by. $sum: 1 counts rows. $avg averages a number. $max and $min pick the high and low value. $push builds an array of the names in that group.
Use: group by role. Admins are Ada and Grace, so the admin row has count 2 and average age 40.5. The member row is only Lin, so count is 1 and average age is 28.
Output: one object for admin and one object for member.
hindi: $group kai documents ko ek _id par jod deta hai. $sum: 1 rows ginta hai. $avg average nikalta hai. $max aur $min badi aur chhoti value chunte hain. $push us group ke naam ki array banata hai.
Use: role par group karo. Admin mein Ada aur Grace hain, isliye count 2 aur average age 40.5 hai. Member mein sirf Lin hai, isliye count 1 aur average 28 hai.
Output: admin ke liye ek object aur member ke liye ek object.

lessons.title: $lookup
english: $lookup joins another collection. from is the other collection name. localField is the field on this document. foreignField is the field on the other collection. as is the new array that holds the matches.
Use: join orders onto users where users.name equals orders.userName. Ada gets two orders, book and pen. Grace gets one order, book. Lin gets an empty orders array because no order uses the name Lin.
Output: Ada's document contains orders with sku book price 12 and sku pen price 3.
hindi: $lookup doosri collection jodta hai. from doosri collection ka naam hai. localField is document ka field hai. foreignField doosri collection ka field hai. as nayi array hai jisme matches aate hain.
Use: users.name ko orders.userName se jodo. Ada ko book aur pen milte hain. Grace ko sirf book milti hai. Lin ki orders array khaali rehti hai.
Output: Ada ke document mein book 12 aur pen 3 hain.

lessons.title: $unwind
english: $unwind splits an array field into one document per element. After lookup, Ada has an orders array of two items. unwind on $orders turns that into two documents. Each document still has the name Ada, and orders is now one object, not an array.
Use preserveNullAndEmptyArrays: true when you still want users who have no orders. Without it, Lin disappears because the orders array is empty. With it, Lin stays and orders is missing or null.
Output: two rows for Ada. The first sku is book at price 12. The second sku is pen at price 3.
hindi: $unwind array ke har element ko alag document bana deta hai. lookup ke baad Ada ke paas do orders hain. unwind unhe do documents bana deta hai. name Ada rehta hai, aur orders ab ek object hota hai, array nahi.
preserveNullAndEmptyArrays: true un users ko bhi rakhta hai jinke orders nahi hain. Bina iske Lin gayab ho jata hai. Iske saath Lin rehta hai.
Output: Ada ki do rows. Pehli book 12, doosri pen 3.

lessons.title: $project
english: $project chooses the fields in the output. 1 keeps a field. 0 drops a field. Do not mix keep and drop in one stage, except _id, which you may drop while keeping other fields. You can also build a new field with $concat, $add, or $multiply.
Use: keep name and role, drop _id, and add a label such as Ada (admin). Age is gone because it was not included.
Output: three objects. Ada (admin), Grace (admin), and Lin (member). None of them includes _id or age.
hindi: $project output ke fields chunta hai. 1 field rakhta hai. 0 field hataata hai. Ek stage mein keep aur drop ek saath mat mix karo. Sirf _id ko drop kar sakte ho. $concat se naya field bhi bana sakte ho.
Use: name aur role rakho, _id hatao, aur label banao jaise Ada (admin). age isliye nahi aati kyunki use include nahi kiya.
Output: teen objects. Ada (admin), Grace (admin), aur Lin (member). Inme _id ya age nahi hai.

lessons.title: $facet
english: $facet runs several pipelines on the same input and returns one document. Each key is a name you choose. The value is that pipeline. Use it when one screen needs two summaries and you do not want two database calls.
Use: admins lists the admin names, and oldest finds the highest age. Both run on Ada, Grace, and Lin. admins contains Ada and Grace. oldest contains 45, which is Grace's age.
Output: one array with a single document. That document has an admins array and an oldest array.
hindi: $facet ek hi input par kai pipelines chalata hai aur ek document deta hai. Har key ek naam hai. Value uski pipeline hai. Jab ek screen ko do summary chahiye, tab ise use karo.
Use: admins admin naam list karta hai, aur oldest sabse badi age nikalta hai. admins mein Ada aur Grace hain. oldest 45 hai, jo Grace ki age hai.
Output: ek document. Usme admins array aur oldest array hai.

lessons.title: Validation methods
english: Schema paths accept required, min, max, minlength, maxlength, enum, and match. match takes a regular expression. enum takes the allowed strings. A custom rule is validate: { validator(value) { return value.includes('@'); }, message: 'Email required' }.

doc.validate() and Model.create run these rules. doc.validateSync() runs them without a promise, which is useful in a test. doc.invalidate(path, message) adds your own error. error.errors[path].message is the text to show the user.

An update does not run validators unless you pass { runValidators: true } to updateOne, updateMany, or findOneAndUpdate. required on an update only fails when the field is present and empty, because the operators do not send the whole document.
Output: User.create({ name: '' }) throws a ValidationError. error.errors.name.kind is minlength or required, depending on the rule you set.
hindi: Schema par required, min, max, minlength, maxlength, enum, aur match lagte hain. Custom rule validate object se lagti hai. doc.validate aur Model.create ye rules chalate hain. doc.validateSync bina promise ke check karta hai. doc.invalidate khud error jodta hai.
Update validators tabhi chalte hain jab { runValidators: true } do. error.errors[path].message user ko dikhane layak text hai.
Output: khali name par User.create ValidationError throw karta hai.

lessons.title: Middleware methods
english: schema.pre(name, function) runs before a hook. schema.post(name, function) runs after. Document hooks include save, validate, deleteOne, and init. Query hooks include find, findOne, updateOne, updateMany, deleteOne, deleteMany, and countDocuments.

In a document hook, this is the document. In a query hook, this is the query. Call this.getFilter() to read the filter. Middleware must be a normal function when you need this. An arrow function does not get this.

pre hooks can be async. Throw, or call next(error), to stop the operation. post('save') is a good place to log the id after a successful write. Do not start a second save of the same document inside pre('save'), or you will recurse.
Output: a pre('save') that sets this.updatedAt makes the saved document's updatedAt a Date. console.log in post('save') prints the new _id.
hindi: schema.pre hook se pehle chalta hai. schema.post baad mein chalta hai. Document hooks save, validate, deleteOne, aur init hain. Query hooks find, findOne, updateOne, updateMany, deleteOne, deleteMany, aur countDocuments hain.
Document hook mein this document hai. Query hook mein this query hai. this ke liye normal function likho, arrow function nahi. pre async ho sakta hai. Throw karoge to operation ruk jaayegi.
Output: pre('save') updatedAt set kare to saved document par Date hoti hai.

lessons.title: Index methods
english: schema.index({ email: 1 }, { unique: true }) declares an index. Put unique: true on the path for a single-field unique index. Model.createIndexes() builds the declared indexes. Model.syncIndexes() creates missing indexes and drops indexes that are no longer on the schema. Model.listIndexes() returns what MongoDB has. Model.cleanIndexes() drops indexes that the schema does not declare.

Model.diffIndexes() tells you which indexes would be created or dropped. Query.hint({ email: 1 }) forces one index for a single query. A unique index makes a second insert of the same email fail with error code 11000.
Output: listIndexes() includes _id_ plus email_1 after createIndexes(). Inserting the same email twice throws MongoServerError with code 11000.
hindi: schema.index index declare karta hai. Path par unique: true ek field ko unique banata hai. Model.createIndexes indexes banata hai. Model.syncIndexes missing indexes banata hai aur purane hataata hai. Model.listIndexes MongoDB ke indexes dikhata hai. Model.cleanIndexes schema se bahar wale indexes hataata hai.
hint ek query ko index chunne par majboor karta hai. Same email do baar insert karoge to code 11000 aata hai.
Output: createIndexes ke baad listIndexes mein email_1 hota hai. Doosri same email par code 11000 aata hai.
